keyFindings.description: handed_over_from defaults to '' for every row that exists at deploy, with no backfill. A child a pre-deploy daemon handed over without its run (no tree_lifecycles row, TakenBack cleared, CarriesRun false) passes RanAsRoot, so the first adoption sweep after the deploy pulls it back into its old root's tree once that root is live — the contract the architect ruled on, broken for existing rows. The adoption sweep is new in this PR, so this cannot happen before the deploy. Existing data marks most of them exactly: every outbox hand-over since #1896 writes processed_events ('outbox', 'handover:<KEY>:<row id>'), which nothing prunes; a hand-over or orphan that ran a worker under its old tree has a claims row with tree <> key. Backfill handed_over_from from those for key = tree rows; name any population no data marks (an uncarried orphan a person admitted that never ran a worker) under 'Not proven / risk' with a pre-deploy query. A generation > 1 heuristic must not be used: it would permanently refuse INFRA-214-style roots that re-admitted themselves.
